UnitStatement: DEL-11-04's primary purpose is to define the setup boundary for future invented-data educational examples used for mechanics-only demonstrations and fake-rule-pack demonstrations.

Future public examples must be original or invented and must not reproduce protected standards text, tables, formulas, examples, allowables, SIF or flexibility data, protected dimensional tables, commercial-software examples, or vendor proprietary data.
The two example families are mechanics-only demonstration examples and fake-rule-pack demonstration examples.
This setup run does not create actual example model files under examples/models/invented/*, tutorials outside this deliverable, source code, schemas, or issued artifacts.
Fake rule-pack examples are fictional non-code teaching devices and must not resemble or approximate real code allowables, formulas, load combinations, or acceptance rules.
Mechanics-only examples may illustrate open centerline mechanics concepts and reproducibility expectations, but must not be presented as design bases or compliance checks.
Future example data must be unit-aware and must carry provenance such as PUBLIC_DOMAIN_OR_ORIGINAL or a stronger documented redistribution basis.
Example outputs are educational and test-support artifacts only; professional reliance requires competent human review outside the software.
If a future example needs code-specific data, leave the value TBD or require user/private input; do not invent a realistic code value.
If a future example would benefit from a real standard example, stop and route to human/legal review; do not copy or paraphrase protected examples into public artifacts.
If a fake rule pack needs pass/fail behavior, use clearly fictional labels and non-engineering placeholder values; avoid code-style formulas and realistic allowables.
If a mechanics-only example needs numeric quantities, use original toy quantities with unit labels and provenance; document that they are not engineering recommendations.
If a tutorial wants to compare against commercial software, exclude the comparison from public examples unless a separate lawful and approved basis exists.
If a future example is used in validation or regression, record the distinction between mechanics verification and code compliance; do not imply professional approval.

This setup artifact defines constraints, acceptance checks, and dependency signals for future invented educational examples without creating external example files, tutorials, code, schemas, private data, or ISSUED artifacts.

Invented educational examples let future users and contributors inspect OpenPipeStress mechanics and rule-pack workflow boundaries without importing protected standards data or implying engineering reliance.
Public examples are invented, original, and clearly non-code.
Mechanics-only examples demonstrate solver workflow and reproducibility, not code acceptance.
Fake-rule-pack examples demonstrate missing-data and rule-check plumbing, not real design rules.
Every future example must carry unit and provenance information.
Missing or unresolved data remains visible as TBD or a finding.
Software examples never certify, approve, seal, or declare professional code compliance.

Mechanics-only examples should be simple enough to audit while showing model identity, units, nodes/elements or comparable centerline entities, supports, load cases, diagnostics, results, and reproducibility metadata.
Any future numeric values should be toy values created for demonstration and not copied from standards, vendor catalogues, owner specifications, or commercial software examples.

Fake-rule-pack demonstrations should show that user-rule checks are separate from mechanics solves, using fictional rule names, fictional required inputs, fake threshold labels, and placeholder outcomes.
Fake-rule-pack demonstrations must not teach or approximate real code formulas, material allowables, stress categories, SIF/flexibility factors, or load-combination rules.
A public invented example can support regression or verification of software behavior, but it is not evidence that any real piping system is safe, compliant, or professionally approved.
Trade-off educational clarity vs realism: prefer auditability and boundary clarity over realistic engineering values.
Trade-off reusable fixture vs hidden default: make invented provenance explicit and keep unresolved data visible.
Trade-off mechanics demonstration vs rule-check demonstration: keep mechanics-only examples separate from fake-rule-pack examples so result status is not confused.
Trade-off public convenience vs IP protection: do not include protected examples or commercial software comparisons for convenience.
Trade-off validation support vs compliance implication: use examples for software behavior checks only and keep professional reliance outside software authority.
